You are fixing two confirmed money bugs in the Nxeon platform at /opt/nxeon (Next.js + Prisma + TypeScript). A test agent found these with failing assertions; both are real. Read the surrounding code carefully before changing anything — this codebase's dominant defect class is "a surface reporting an outcome it never verified", so prefer fixes that make the invariant checkable over fixes that paper over the symptom.

BUG 1 — Upgrade/downgrade proration cap asymmetry. Money is destroyed on a round trip.
`lib/resize.ts:83` calls `remainingMonths(server.expiresAt, Date.now())` with NO cap, while `lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts:189` passes `server.termMonths` as the cap. With a stacked `expiresAt` (a customer who hit "Renew now" repeatedly, so expiry is 36 months out on a 12-month term), a Starter↔Max upgrade-then-downgrade charges $544.32 and credits only $181.44 — the platform keeps $362.88 that it did not earn.
The failing assertion, verbatim:
  assert.equal(
    prorateUpgradeCents({from:899,to:3299,termMonths:12,monthsRemaining:remainingMonths(stacked,now),promo}),
    prorateDowngradeCreditCents({from:3299,to:899,termMonths:12,monthsRemaining:remainingMonths(stacked,now,12),promo})
  )  // → 54432 !== 18144
Both call sites' client-side pickers agree with their own server, so this is a genuine design asymmetry, not display drift. Decide which cap is CORRECT and make both sides use it. My read: the customer genuinely paid for all the months in `expiresAt`, so the uncapped figure is the honest one for BOTH directions — but verify that against how `remainingMonths` and `lib/proration.ts` are actually used, and against whether an uncapped credit can be abused (a customer who stacks 36 months, upgrades, then downgrades must not be able to extract more than they paid). Whichever way you go, the invariant that must hold afterwards is: upgrade charge and the mirror-image downgrade credit are equal, and a credit never exceeds what was actually paid. Also fix the client-side picker on whichever side you change, so the displayed number still equals the charged/credited number.

BUG 2 — Sub-floor card leg reaches Stripe and the API rejects the charge.
`lib/wallet-split.ts:52` can only lift the card leg to the 50c Stripe minimum when `dueCents >= 50`. For `{dueCents:30, balanceCents:10, useWallet:true}` it returns `cardCents: 20` with `clampedForStripeMin: false`. `lib/actions-server.ts:148` and `lib/actions-disk.ts:85` hand that straight to `createResizeCheckout`/`createDiskExpandCheckout` with no floor guard — contrast `lib/stripe-cards.ts:523`, which DOES check. Reachable in practice via a few-cent resize proration late in a term. The failing assertion:
  assert.ok(walletSplit({dueCents:30,balanceCents:10,useWallet:true}).cardCents >= STRIPE_MIN_CENTS)  // → 20
Fix it where it belongs. When the total due is itself below the Stripe minimum, the right behaviour is almost certainly to take the whole thing from the wallet if the wallet covers it, and otherwise to not attempt a card charge at all rather than to inflate what the customer owes — but read `lib/wallet-split.ts` in full and pick the behaviour that is consistent with the rest of the file's contract, and make sure `clampedForStripeMin` accurately reflects what happened (the deploy wizard prints a line based on it).

There is an existing test suite at /opt/nxeon/test/ (node:test, run with `npm test`). `test/proration.test.ts` and `test/wallet-split.test.ts` already exist and encode these invariants — `test/wallet-split.test.ts` has a test explicitly marked as documenting bug 2 as a KNOWN GAP. Update those tests to assert the CORRECT behaviour (turn the known-gap test into a real assertion), and add a case for the stacked-expiry round trip.

Then verify, and only report what you actually observed:
  cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep -vE '^test/[^ ]+\.test\.ts\([0-9]+,[0-9]+\): error TS5097:'
  cd /opt/nxeon && npm test
Do NOT run `npm run build` or deploy — I am editing worker/migrate-real.ts concurrently and will build and deploy everything together. Do not touch worker/migrate-real.ts, worker/migrate-detect.ts, tsconfig.json, or package.json.

Report: what you changed and why, the invariant each fix establishes, the test output you actually saw, and anything you found that you did NOT fix.

/**
 * Months of paid term left at `now` — 0 when there is no expiry (free/admin
 * servers) and clamped at zero so an already-expired term never prorates
 * negatively.
 *
 * There is deliberately NO cap parameter, and re-adding one would reopen a money
 * bug. `expiresAt` only ever moves forward in exchange for payment: the initial
 * order term (lib/order.ts, lib/actions.ts placeOrder), `renewNow`
 * (lib/actions.ts) and the auto-renew sweep (worker/billing.ts) each advance it by
 * exactly `termMonths` and charge `vpsTermPriceCents` for those months. So every
 * month between `now` and `expiresAt` is a month the customer has actually bought,
 * however many terms of "Renew now" are stacked up in there, and the honest
 * prorated figure covers all of them.
 *
 * This used to take `capMonths`, and that optional knob is precisely how the two
 * directions drifted apart: the upgrade path (lib/resize.ts) passed no cap while
 * the downgrade path (lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts) passed `server.termMonths`.
 * A customer who had stacked "Renew now" out to 36 months on a 12-month term was
 * charged $544.32 to move Starter -> Max and credited only $181.44 to move
 * straight back — the platform kept $362.88 it never earned. Four call sites
 * (two servers, two pickers) had to agree on that argument by convention, and they
 * did not. With the knob gone every caller gets the same number from the same
 * one-argument call, so the round-trip invariant is structural instead of a
 * comment someone has to honour.
 *
 * A cap was never what protected the credit side either. The credit is
 * `(effective(from) - effective(to)) x months` priced through `prorateDeltaCents`
 * at the term-discounted AND promo-reduced rate, while the renewal paths charge
 * the term price with no promo applied — so the credit for a given month is
 * strictly less than what that month cost. What made the old credit a money
 * printer was the RAW LIST-price delta it used before 2026-07-25, not the number
 * of months it spanned.
 */
export function remainingMonths(expiresAt: Date | null, now: number): number {
  if (!expiresAt) return 0;
  return Math.max(0, (expiresAt.getTime() - now) / MS_PER_AVG_MONTH);
}

Both bugs fixed. Report:

## BUG 1 — proration cap asymmetry

**Decision: uncapped is correct for both directions.** I verified your read rather than assuming it. `expiresAt` only ever moves forward in exchange for payment — the initial order term (`lib/order.ts`, `lib/actions.ts` `placeOrder`), `renewNow` (`lib/actions.ts:611`) and the auto-renew sweep (`worker/billing.ts:477`) each advance it by exactly `termMonths` and charge `vpsTermPriceCents` for those months. So every month between now and `expiresAt` is a month the customer bought.

On abuse: an uncapped credit is `(eff(from) − eff(to)) × months`, structurally less than `eff(from) × months`, and the renewal paths charge the term price with **no promo** while proration credits the promo-reduced rate — so the credit per month is strictly below what that month cost. I checked this numerically at 36/72/108 stacked months, with and without a promo.

The old test's "unclamped is free money" claim was the actual error: it bounded a **108-month** credit against **one term's** payment. Wrong denominator — a customer 108 months out on a 36-month term paid three terms. That bad bound is what justified the cap.

**Fix — removed the `capMonths` parameter entirely** rather than syncing four call sites. The optional knob *was* the defect: two servers and two pickers had to agree on it by convention and didn't. Now nobody can express a different duration.
- `lib/proration.ts` — param removed, doc rewritten with the reasoning
- `lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts:189` — cap argument dropped
- `components/customer/ResizeDown.tsx:73` — client picker, cap dropped (the display side of the half I changed)
- `lib/resize.ts` — comment explaining why the charge side must *stay* uncapped (capping it alone would mint money)

**Invariant established:** all four call sites make a byte-identical two-argument call, and upgrade charge == downgrade credit for every term × stacked-expiry combination. Your assertion now yields `54432 === 54432`.

## BUG 2 — sub-floor card leg

Fixed in `lib/wallet-split.ts` — the one function that owns the floor — not by bolting guards onto the call sites. New early return for `0 < dueCents < 50`: `cardCents: 0`, `walletApplied: dueCents`, `belowStripeMin: true`. I took your steer against inflating the card to 50c; the customer must never owe more than the quote.

Two things worth flagging in the design:
- **It fires even when `useWallet` is false.** A 30c card charge doesn't exist as an option, so honouring the toggle would leave *no payable split at all*. The hard external constraint wins over the preference, and the flag reports it.
- **I added a distinct `belowStripeMin` field rather than reusing `clampedForStripeMin`.** The flags mean opposite things, and the wizard's clamped line reads "we'll charge {cardCents} to your card" — reusing it would print "$0.00". A test now asserts they're mutually exclusive.

`walletApplied` may exceed the balance in this state. That's not a funding claim — I confirmed every debit on these paths goes through `debitWallet` (`lib/wallet.ts:16`), a guarded `updateMany` with `balanceCents: { gte: cents }`, so a short balance produces "Insufficient balance — top up your wallet first" (already caught by both actions) instead of a Stripe API throw. `ResizePicker` and `AddStorage` now print an honest line that distinguishes "comes out of your wallet" from "top up to at least $X first" based on the real balance. Also removed the now-redundant `dueCents >= STRIPE_MIN_CENTS` from the clamp condition and replaced two hardcoded `fmtMoney(50)` with `STRIPE_MIN_CENTS`. `DeployWizard` left alone — a deploy's due is a full term price and can't go sub-floor.

- **`proration.test.ts`**: rewrote the credit bound against a per-month "what was actually paid" denominator; added the stacked-expiry round-trip regression (asserts `up === down === 54432` and pins the old 18144 / $362.88 hole); replaced the `capMonths` test with one asserting the parameter is gone (arity + stray third arg inert); rewrote the four-call-site tripwire to require identical calls.

Promos rotate by calendar date from the ~10% Launch Sale up to 45% (Cyber Monday). Upgrade during a deep promo (small charge), downgrade during a shallow one (large credit), and the customer extracts the spread × delta × months. My symmetry fix only guarantees equality when both legs price against the *same* promo. Properly fixing it needs the effective rate persisted on the server row — a schema change, which I left to you.
